questions.q: What does running terraform init do?
options: Compiles HCL into a binary executable
Downloads the required provider plugins and locks their exact versions
Deletes all existing infrastructure
Creates a new Azure subscription
questions.explain: terraform init reads the required_providers block, downloads the matching provider plugins, and writes a .terraform.lock.hcl file pinning exact versions.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the .terraform.lock.hcl file?
options: It is a backup copy of the state file
It pins the exact provider versions used, so every machine and CI run behaves identically
It stores cloud credentials in plain text
It prevents terraform apply from ever running
questions.explain: The lock file ensures consistent provider behavior across every teammate's machine and every CI run by pinning exact downloaded versions.

questions.q: How does the azurerm provider authenticate in this lesson's setup?
options: By emailing HashiCorp for a token
By using whatever Azure CLI session is already active after running az login
By hardcoding a username and password in the .tf file
It does not require any authentication
questions.explain: The azurerm provider reuses the Azure CLI's existing login session, so no secrets need to be written into the Terraform configuration.

questions.q: Why is the empty features {} block required in the azurerm provider configuration?
options: It enables billing alerts
It stores the Azure subscription ID
It confirms you are intentionally using the version 3.x feature set, even with no custom settings
It is purely decorative and has no effect
questions.explain: The azurerm provider requires a features block (even empty) as an explicit acknowledgment of its version 3.x behavior.

questions.q: How does the aws provider in this lesson obtain its credentials?
options: By sharing the azurerm provider's authentication
From a named AWS CLI profile set up with aws configure, referenced in the provider block
It automatically generates its own credentials
From a hardcoded access key inside the .tf file
questions.explain: The aws provider reads credentials the same way the AWS CLI does, here via a named profile created with aws configure and referenced in the provider block's profile argument.
